meaning: A fake pop-up warning that says your device is infected. It scares you into paying for a useless fix or downloading something harmful.
clues: It involves a program or a message on your device.
It is designed to frighten you.
A loud pop-up says your device is full of viruses, though no scan was ever run, and tells you to click or pay.
The warning is fake. The "fix" it sells may do nothing, or may bring in real harm.
It has nine letters and starts with S. The first part is the feeling it tries to give you.
assumes: Ransomware locks your files and demands payment
Spyware secretly watches what you do

decoys.meaning: Harmful software that locks your files. The crook then demands payment to unlock them.
Hidden software that secretly watches what you do on a device and sends it to someone else.
Software that scans a device for harmful programs and removes them.

exchange.speaker: bud
exchange.text: A pop-up that screams about viruses is probably scareware. Do not tap anything inside it. Just close the tab or app.

exchange.speaker: floyd
exchange.text: Back in my day, the only thing that beeped at me was the microwave.

sources.name: FTC, How To Spot, Avoid, and Report Tech Support Scams

blank.sentence: A pop-up warned me my device was infected and scared me into paying for a useless fix. That was ___.

why: It scares you into paying for a useless fix or a harmful download.
